lines.text: Das ist übrigens der Tag, auf den du alles verschoben hast.
lines.note: The screen points at tomorrow as the day the reader keeps postponing everything to; a reveal-style take on the postponing idea the owner liked but vetoed twice for having no punch, true under any weather.

lines.text: Mich schaust du dir jeden Abend an. Die Zahnseide nie.
lines.note: Evening-routine hygiene jab: the reader checks the screen every night but never the floss; needs no weather, so it fits every pool.

lines.text: Ich seh ja, wie's bei dir aussieht. Da red ich lieber übers Wetter.
lines.note: The screen has seen the state of the reader's home and would rather stick to small talk about the weather, which ties back to whatever forecast sits above it.

lines.text: Wir sind beide keine großen Leuchten. Bei mir hat's wenigstens technische Gründe.
lines.note: Idiom 'keine große Leuchte' (not very bright): the e-ink screen with no backlight admits it is dim too but has a technical excuse, and the reader has none.

lines.text: Ich lauf wochenlang mit einer Akkuladung. Du schnaufst schon im zweiten Stock.
lines.note: Screen versus reader on stamina: one battery charge lasts the screen weeks, and the reader is out of breath by the second floor; a true device fact, weather-free.

lines.text: Dein Horoskop für morgen erspar ich dir.
lines.note: The screen gives tomorrow's weather but kindly spares the reader their horoscope; a short fate jab that works under good and bad tomorrows alike.

lines.text: An manchen sieht ein Schirm elegant aus. An dir wie geklaut.
lines.note: Every rain and wet-start sentence names the umbrella; on some people it looks elegant, on the reader it looks stolen, and nobody gets wet.

lines.text: Aufgespannt braucht der Schirm fast so viel Platz wie du.
lines.note: Size jab: an open umbrella takes up almost as much room as the reader; fits every rain sentence without predicting a soaking.

lines.text: Wie bei allen, die dich näher kennenlernen.
lines.note: Tomorrow cools off the way everyone does once they get to know the reader; strongest under the warm-start sentence and true under all three (social rejection, not the vetoed huddling frame).

lines.text: Zwiebellook ist angesagt. Bei dir passt sogar der Geruch.
lines.note: The weather-report phrase for layering days, turned on the reader's smell; holds for any colder day, from T-shirt to sweater up to winter coat (risk: 'Zwiebelprinzip' was in two vetoed On lines, as a weak 'they call it X' gag).

lines.text: Wie eine Schaufensterpuppe. Bloß ohne die Figur.
lines.note: One outfit all day, like a shop-window mannequin but without the mannequin's figure; a body jab that builds on the steady sentence without repeating it.

lines.text: Die Wärme reizt ihre Gleitzeit mal wieder voll aus.
lines.note: Warmth that turns up later in the day is an office worker using every minute of flexitime; about the weather, and it works whether warmer means mild or hot (nearest live idea: the 'Durchsage' line about warmth being delayed).

lines.text: Diesmal kommt die Wärme wenigstens ohne Nebenkostenabrechnung.
lines.note: The Grantler's grudging plus about the world: this warmth comes without a utility bill; holds whether warmer means pleasant or hot.

lines.text: Ein Tag wie eine Koalition: für jeden was dabei, zufrieden ist keiner.
lines.note: A day that starts cooler and ends warmer is like a coalition, with something for everyone and nobody happy; neutral on mild and hot days alike.
